name: Xerénte
confidence_why: 6 independent first-hand descriptions agree (5 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

new_statements.quote: 1.4. A sílaba tônica é sempre a última da palavra. [pa'di] 'tamanduá' [da'pra] 'pé' [pse'di] 'é bom'. Nos casos onde a vogal final se perde ou está em processo de se perder, a sílaba tônica é a nova sílaba última. [mãto watÍ'brÍ] ou [mãto wa'tÍbr] 'ele saiu' [kuta'bi] 'realmente' [kutabi + di] ––> [ku'tabÊdÊ] 'é real'
new_statements.translation: 1.4. The stressed syllable is always the last one of the word. [pa'di] 'anteater' [da'pra] 'foot' [pse'di] 'is good'. In cases where the final vowel is lost or is in the process of being lost, the stressed syllable is the new last syllable. [mãto watÍ'brÍ] or [mãto wa'tÍbr] 'he went out' [kuta'bi] 'really' [kutabi + di] --> [ku'tabÊdÊ] 'is real'
new_statements.citation: Mattos, Rinaldo de (1971). Fonêmica Xerente. Série Lingüística N 1. Brasília. pp. 79-100.
new_statements.locator: §1.4 'A sílaba tônica', p. 2 of the SIL 2003 web re-edition ('SL-1 Xerente ', 15 pp.); original Série Lingüística pagination (pp. 79-100) not recoverable from this copy. Souza (2008) cites the same passage as 'Mattos (1973, p. 2)'.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (extracted text, 15 pp., text present). §1.4 is on p. 2, lines: '1.4. A sílaba tônica é sempre a última da palavra. [pa'di] 'tamanduá' [da'pra] 'pé' [pse'di] 'é bom' / Nos casos onde a vogal final se perde ou está em processo de se perder, a sílaba tônica é a nova sílaba última. [mãto watÍ'brÍ] ou [mãto wa'tÍbr] 'ele saiu' [kuta'bi] 'realmente'' — then the page-2 footer, and the last example '[kutabi + di] ––> [ku'tabÊdÊ] 'é real'' sits at the top of p. 3 (the compiler 'p. 2' locator is right for the rule sentence; only the final example spills onto p. 3). The quote otherwise matches character for character. A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole text for tônica/acento/tom/…
new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record (an earlier compilation-2026-08-31) gives final stress = fixed final; Mattos states exactly that ('sempre a última da palavra'). This work is the primary source that Souza 2008, Cotrim 2016 and Grannier 2010 all cite for the final-stress rule.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the word, without exception; when a word-final vowel has been lost (the language is undergoing extensive vowel loss), stress moves to the syllable that has become the new final syllable. Stress is predictable and not marked in the phonemic transcription.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions. The vowel-loss cases are presented as the same rule applied to the new final syllable; in the example [kutabi + di] -> [ku'tabÊdÊ] the stress surfaces on the syllable before the non-phonemic transitional vowels [Ê], i.e. on the syllable that is phonemically final after the loss of /i/.
new_statements.identity_note: Mattos describes the Xerente spoken in seven villages between the Tocantins and Sono rivers (then Goiás, now Tocantins), data 1964-1966, main consultant Anjo dos Santos; ~500 speakers at the time. No dialect split is discussed; this is the same variety (Akwẽ-Xerente) treated in all later work. The Xavante comparison in §1 concerns the sister language, not a Xerente dialect.

tone_statements.quote: Na seção 2.1.3 faz-se uma referência a Dixon (2010), quando descreve o acento como um dos sistemas prosódicos que se manifesta na sílaba da maioria das línguas que não possuem um sistema contrastivo de tom. Esse é também o caso do Akwẽ-Xerente, cujo acento tem sido qualificado de previsível (MATTOS, 1973), demarcativo e não-distintivo (BRAGGIO, 2005), e pós-lexical (SOUZA, 2008). A observação de palavras isoladas do corpus confirma, na maioria dos casos, o aspecto previsível do acento na língua, o qual recai geralmente sobre a última sílaba da palavra.
tone_statements.translation: In section 2.1.3 reference is made to Dixon (2010), who describes stress as one of the prosodic systems manifested on the syllable in most languages that do not have a contrastive tone system. This is also the case of Akwẽ-Xerente, whose stress has been characterised as predictable (Mattos 1973), demarcative and non-distinctive (Braggio 2005), and post-lexical (Souza 2008). Observation of isolated words from the corpus confirms, in most cases, the predictable character of stress in the language, which generally falls on the last syllable of the word.

tone_statements.n_tones: None: not a tone language (no contrastive tone system)

(2) Deciding source is a 2008 phonology MA thesis resting on Mattos 1973 (SIL phonemic sketch, fieldwork 1964-66), whose sec. 1.4 says the same thing; I opened Mattos and four later descriptions (Braggio 2005, Sousa Filho 2007, Grannier 2010, Cotrim 2016) and all state fixed word-final stress, with the only nuances being (a) stress stays final under suffixation and (b) where younger speakers drop the final vowel the new final syllable is stressed — both consistent with fixed: final syllable coding.
